A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conjuring Semantic Similarity by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion similarity correlations on STS/SICK-R, ablations in Figure 3 and Table 2, and generated-image case studies, including Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds diffusion-baseline results in Table 1 and RG65/SimLex word-similarity results in Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the proposed trajectory-based distance remain unchanged. Replacing 'either' with 'both' prompts in Section 3.2 clarifies the two trajectories already present in v1's algorithm. The newly evaluated variants are comparison baselines.

E1.justification: v2 adds RG65 and SimLex-999, extending sentence benchmarks and small qualitative word examples to systematic human-annotated word-similarity evaluation covering nouns, adjectives and verbs. Existing STS/SICK-R coverage and qualitative cases are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Initial Timestep Prediction, Final Timestep Prediction, Direct Output Comparison and Conjuring Semantic Similarity (KL-Div). These introduce direct comparisons within Stable Diffusion alongside the retained embedding and language-model comparators. Endpoint ablations existed previously, but these comparators were absent from v1's Table 1.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce baseline comparisons using common parameters and Monte Carlo sampling, plus Spearman evaluation stratified by part of speech against the text encoder. Existing STS/SICK-R settings, guidance scale, scheduler and T = 10 are unchanged; the hardware statement is newly disclosed information.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and new Table 2 add quantitative error analysis of how semantic alignment differs between the text encoder and generator across parts of speech. The KL-only comparison additionally tests symmetrization. Earlier timestep, sampling-budget and model-choice ablations and Appendix A cases are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard deviation across datasets, and the Monte Carlo sampling ablation remains unchanged. New baseline rows use the same reporting practice; no seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance procedures are added.

E6.justification: The proposed method's Table 1 average remains 65.4 ± 5.3, while four added baselines report averages of 53.0, 56.9, 51.3 and 64.0. New Table 2 reports word-level results, including SimLex verb correlations of 10.3 for the encoder and -14.3 for StableDiffusion. The original denoising-step results are retained as Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds formal definitions of comparison distances, including the distance between outputs generated from shared initial noise. The original SDE assumptions, Girsanov derivation and proposed distance remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the original similarity, interpretability and semantic-alignment claims. Section 5 adds fine-grained identification of diffusion-model failure modes as an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the word analysis as preservation of noun semantics alongside deterioration of adjective and verb semantics during diffusion learning. Table 2 supports the verb deficit more clearly than preferential noun preservation over adjectives. Existing abstraction, encoder-bottleneck and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly reports a single RTX 4090 GPU and approximately 2.0 seconds per Monte Carlo step. Section 4.2 documents implementing the baselines with Monte Carlo sampling and the proposed method's parameters. These additions do not establish changes to existing experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hill et al. (2015) and Rubenstein and Goodenough (1965) for the word benchmarks. It also explicitly distinguishes semantic-alignment evaluation from generation quality and diversity metrics. The broader related-work discussion and cited comparison methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 gains a Baselines subsection, Ablations becomes Empirical Analysis, and the concluding paragraph is expanded. Local wording corrections and explanatory additions accompany these changes, while most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from side-by-side trajectories to stacked panels with clearer labels and additional intermediate snapshots. Table 1 gains baseline rows, a word-analysis table is added, and the previous Table 2 becomes Table 3. These are localized changes; Figures 2–5 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the direct diffusion baselines better establish the value of the proposed distance, and the word analysis provides useful evidence of verb failures. Hardware/runtime disclosure and the redesigned Figure 1 also improve transparency. The net gain is limited by the new analysis's weak support for its claimed preferential preservation of nouns over adjectives.
